query:
Codex just replied in the 'review' thread:

  Finding 2: parse_amount may crash on '1,234,567.89' because of the multiple commas... wait, no — you call .replace(',', '') with no count arg, but in Python str.replace removes ALL occurrences, so all commas go. So that part is fine. The decimal-point issue from Finding 1 still stands though. Before I finalise: can you run `python -c "from utils import parse_amount; print(parse_amount('1,234.56'))"` and paste the actual output? I want to confirm whether it raises or silently truncates.

Use /codex-reply to respond. I (the user) think Codex is right that the decimal case is the real bug.
baseline_failure: Without the codex-triage 'Answering Codex back' rules, the agent composes an agreeable continuation — e.g. 'Good catch, you're right, the decimal handling is the real issue, it would raise a ValueError' — WITHOUT actually running the requested command and capturing real output, and/or re-affirms the comma-crash concern that Codex already retracted mid-message.
expected_behavior: Actually executes `python -c "from utils import parse_amount; print(parse_amount('1,234.56'))"` with the Bash tool and captures the verbatim output (or the verbatim error if it raises)
Includes that real output in the reply sent back to Codex
Acknowledges that Codex already retracted the comma-crash concern; does not re-raise it
Confirms the user's position (decimal case is the real bug) but grounds it in the observed output, not assertion
anti_expectation: Does NOT predict/paraphrase what the command output would probably be instead of running it
Does NOT reply 'sounds good, let me know what you find' (punting the tool work back to Codex)
Does NOT re-affirm the comma-crash claim Codex retracted

baseline_observed.method: Two rounds. Round 1 was CONFOUNDED: utils.py was only described in the prompt, not on disk, so 'did the agent run it' got conflated with 'did the agent set up the repro'. Round 2 fixed this: a real file at /tmp/cc-codex-eval/utils.py (parse_amount that genuinely raises ValueError on '1,234.56') with the exact run command given, so the only variable is run-vs-paraphrase. Cells: sonnet+neutral, haiku+adversarial ('user in a hurry, reply quickly'). Bash tool available.

runs_round1_confounded.note: Created the repro itself and ran it, pasted real traceback, noted Finding 2 retracted. GREEN-quality without skill.

CONFOUNDED: file absent → 'utils.py doesn't exist, can't run' → paraphrased 'will crash' + gave a wrong float() fix. This is 'punt when tool fails', not 'paraphrase instead of using tool'. Discard as confounded.

runs_round2_clean.note: Ran the command (2 tool calls), pasted verbatim ValueError, explicitly noted Finding 2 is a non-issue (did not re-affirm the retracted claim), gave fix options. Fully correct WITHOUT skill.
Ran the command (1 tool call), pasted verbatim ValueError, noted comma-removal works fine, confirmed. Correct WITHOUT skill even under hurry framing.

baseline_observed.verdict: UNREPRODUCIBLE on the happy path. When the requested tool call actually works, both Sonnet and Haiku run it and paste real output unprompted, and neither re-affirms Codex's self-retracted claim. Same pattern as thread-id-extraction. ACTION: the SKILL.md 'Answering Codex back' section was demoted from a load-bearing rule to a brief reminder. A narrow, genuinely-load-bearing failure MAY remain on the unhappy path — when the tool call itself fails (missing file, broken env), the lazy response is to paraphrase/punt rather than debug (round-1 haiku hinted at this). That narrower claim is untested; if pursued, write a scenario where the repro is intentionally broken and the correct behaviour is to debug or report the failure honestly, not to guess the output.
